events.description: SCC meeting on Soviet forces in Afghanistan: CIA assessment of ~40,000 Soviet troops, Egyptian equipment for insurgents via Pakistan, aid to Pakistan and non-proliferation issues.
Agreement to seek an NSC meeting later in the week on larger regional strategic questions arising from the Soviet intervention.
SCC meeting on Soviet forces in Afghanistan, 9:30-10:30 a.m.
CIA reported about 40,000 Soviet troops in Afghanistan, Afghan army desertions, and expected insurgent resistance growing in spring.
CIA reported Egypt sending equipment to Pakistan for Afghan insurgents.
Warren Christopher reported on his NAC trip and urged a standing mechanism for coordinating allied responses.
Agreed to raise Pakistan aid and nonproliferation exception at NSC meeting that day, and to seek a later NSC meeting that week on broader strategic issues.

key_claims: CIA assessed about 40,000 Soviet troops were in Afghanistan, facing some resistance.
The Afghan army was shrinking rapidly due to desertions, leaving Soviet forces as the main counterinsurgency force.
Rebel tribes were expected to retreat to the mountains and intensify resistance in spring.
Insurgent strength depends on covert support through Pakistan and Soviet pressure on Pakistan to block it.
Egypt was sending equipment to Pakistan for the Afghan insurgents.
Pakistan's ability to resist Soviet pressure depends on US assistance, complicated by non-proliferation law.
